entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

The Foreman is too slow to see it. You shuffle to the door like a beaten man, and the cloaks watch your hobbles instead of your hands. You bawl the lie through the oak in Goblin, flat and loud: Greyshaft's books are honest, honest as the knife at your sister's throat. Then you tell them to come and break the door, and your chained fists come down on the lantern.

It goes off the desk and bursts. The oil runs out in a bright sheet across the flags, and the Foreman, who is quick for a soft man, throws himself back from it, and the fire misses his sleeve by a hand's breadth. Every cloak in the room is staring at the flames. Tessa uses the moment. Her hairpin clicks, the ring lock falls open, and she is across the room and at your wrist before the first sword comes up. One cuff pops loose. Then the cloaks are on you.

Cloak A's pommel finds the same ridge of bone for the fourth time, and this one is a clean hit. Cloak B drops your sister as she turns. The last thing you see is the oil guttering out on the stone and the Foreman straightening his apron with a hand that shakes.

You wake on the floor with one wrist free and the other still in iron. It is about eleven in the morning, and you have 1 hit point. The fire is a black scorch across the flags and the lantern is a twist of tin. The door is still barred and braced. Behind it, muffled, a heavy ram or shoulder thumps twice and stops, and Dreg's voice swears at it.

Tessa lies a pace from you with her chest rising. Two cloaks stand over her. The Foreman has retreated to his desk and sits very still, and his voice, when it comes, is the thinnest you have heard it.

"You have cost me a lantern, Emberhide, and a morning, and I now have two choices, neither of them tidy. I can hang you both from my own window, or I can open that door and trade you for the walk out. Gorrak Vael has offered me the second." He rubs his beads between finger and thumb. "He is, I am told, willing to leave my ledger alone. For a price. You have until I finish this thought to decide whether I believe him."

He waits for you to speak. What does Korvash do?

His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. input.add_to_description: DEAD, Day 21 ~10:00 AM: Korvash smashed the lantern on the desk; burning oil caught the Foreman's sleeve (failed Dex save) and he burned to death in the ledger-house. The grey cloaks (six) broke and stood down. Tessa picked her wall-ring lock. The key chain and the scorched ledger's chest (in the barred bedchamber) are now unguarded.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You shuffle to the door and say it in Goblin, flat as a hanged man: Greyshaft's books are honest, honest as the knife at your sister's throat. It's a poor lie. You hear how poor it is, and so does he. The Foreman's eyes narrow, and he has the beginning of a word in his mouth.

You don't give him the rest. Your chained fists come down on the lantern, and it bursts across the desk. Burning oil runs over the wood, over the floor, over the Foreman's sleeve. He tries to twist away, but he's slow, and it takes him. He doesn't scream. He goes down on one knee, beating at his arm with the other hand, and the small gentle voice says, almost puzzled, "That is not tidy," and does not say anything after that.

The grey cloaks watch him burn. Nobody moves to put him out. The man at Tessa's neck has taken the blade away without knowing he has done it. The crossbows have come off the shutters. Then the nearest cloak sets down his spear, and the next, and the rest follow, quiet as men setting down a load.

Behind the chair, Tessa's hairpin turns, and the wall ring springs open. She crosses the room at a run and reaches you before the smoke does, with her cut lip and her bruised skull and her hands shaking, and she doesn't say anything. She just puts her forehead against your chest.

Dreg's men come through the door when the cloaks lift the bar. The stair is full of hobgoblins in red-and-tin, and Brun is at the front with his spear held upright and his face wet. Gorrak limps in behind them with Krell on his arm, and stops at what is left of the desk. The fire has been smothered with a cloak. The Foreman is a dark shape on the boards, and at his belt the key chain still hangs, blackened. Through the narrow door to the bedchamber, the bar is still down.

It's a little after ten in the morning on the day after midwinter's eve. You've earned a hundred experience points, and you stand at 1 hit point with the iron still on your wrists. Gorrak is looking at the dead man's belt, then at the barred door, and then at you. The ledger, with his number in it, lies behind that door.

What does Korvash do?

entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You shout it at the gap in the door, flat and cold, a hanged man's voice: *Greyshaft's books are honest, Sergeant, now come and break this door.* On the last word your chained fists come down on the lantern, and it bursts across the desk's edge. Burning oil runs over the Foreman's sleeve and across the flags, between him and his cloaks.

The room screams. The Foreman claws at his arm and backs into the door, and two cloaks drop their bows to beat at him with their cloaks. For half a heartbeat nobody is looking at you. Then a flat of steel comes down on your shoulder and a second blow takes you across the temple, and you go under.

You come back slowly, on your back, to a smell of scorched cloth and wet char, and to daylight. It is nearly two in the afternoon, and you have 1 hit point. The door lies off its hinges. The desk is blackened, and the burn on the Foreman's chair is a long brown tongue. Hobgoblins in the Tally-sworn iron and red stand along the walls. The grey cloaks are on their knees in a row with their hands on their heads, and Dreg's thick-necked bulk stands over them, one forearm wrapped in a bloody rag.

Tessa is kneeling at your side with a wet cloth. Her wrist is raw where the iron was, but she is free, and she is crying and laughing at once. "You *idiot*," she says, "you magnificent *idiot*. Brun was through the door with an axe before the oil had finished burning."

The Foreman sits against the far wall, his right arm bandaged to the shoulder, his face grey, his soft hands bound before him. He is alive. The beads are gone. The chest from the bedchamber stands open on the desk, and Gorrak Vael is bent over it, bare-faced, with the scorched ledger open under his hand. Krell sits beside him, one eye swollen shut, holding a lamp. Gorrak is not reading. He has found his own line, and he is looking at it. He doesn't look up when you stir.

You are at 1 hit point, with your sister at your side and the book open on the desk. Whatever happens to it next is a choice, and everyone in the room is waiting to see who makes it. What does Korvash do?

You shuffle to the door in your hobbles, a beaten man doing as he's told, and put your mouth to the gap. You say it flat and loud in Goblin: Greyshaft's books are honest, honest as the knife at your sister's throat, spoken from a cold heart and a full belly. Now come and break the door.

The lantern skids across the desk with its shutter clanging and stays upright, the oil unspilled. Before you can try again, the nearest cloak's pommel comes down on the ridge of bone above your ear, and the floor takes you.

You come back slowly, an hour later, at 1 hit point. It is just before eleven in the morning. The cold cloth is on your eyes again.

The room has changed little. The four bows are still at the shutters. The Foreman has taken his chair and counted nothing aloud for a long while. He looks pleased, which is worse than angry. Tessa still sits on her stool with her wrist in iron. Her hairpin is hidden in her fist, and the lock on the ring has a bright scratch around it. She is a few turns of the wire from free. The blade at her throat is steady.

Through the door you can hear the stair. The beating of spears has stopped. Dreg's voice comes now in short, flat questions, and a cloak answers each one in the Foreman's soft Goblin through the gap. Your shout reached them, and they have heard the words. They have also heard the way you said them. The sergeant is not storming the door. He is waiting for a sign.

"Your sergeant is a careful man," the Foreman says, without looking at you. "He's weighing a confession that sounds like a taunt against a hanging he saw stopped. I could ask no more of him." He turns his beads. "I'll give you one more chance to say it plainly. Slowly. At the door, so that he can't mistake it."

You have 1 hit point and iron on your wrists. The Tallies are one clear word from either storming the door or going home. Your sister's lock is nearly picked. What does Korvash do?

time: 12 minutes later: Day 27, 7:15:06 AM

You drop behind a boulder, out of the archers' line, and shout your terms down the slope: archers called off, you and Brakk alone at the ford-stones with blades and shields. If you put him down, he and his nine lay down their arms and walk to Harrowmere. If he beats you, your spears go home and the barrel is his.

The quiet stretches. Then Brakk laughs, short and dry, and answers in Goblin. "Terms I can count. Done." He barks an order. The two on the roof lower their bows, though not far.

You watch him while he speaks, and you read him true. The duel he means to keep. The terms are a gift to him, and he is too patient a man to spoil a gift. But a hand goes up to the roof, two fingers, and the archer at the left corner nods. Your spears are not to move. If they do, he will loose.

You whistle two notes back toward the gully. Ushk comes up the goat-path at a crouching run and drops beside you, breathing hard. He sees the yard, and you see his jaw tighten at the sight of the big shape with the ring in its ear. "Witness," you tell him. He nods. "I'll see it all," he says.

You check yourself the way Dargan taught you: breath in the chest, rage ready in the belly, the axe light in your hands. Tessa's three knots are tight on your wrist. Hale and the six spears hold the road behind, still hidden, still silent.

Below, Brakk walks out of the yard alone, longsword in his right hand and round shield on his left arm, to the humped ford-stones. He sets his back to nothing now, in open ground, and waits. His men watch from the wall. It is a quarter past seven, the sun is full on the ford, and the stream runs black and loud.
